implementation_notes: The BCL supplies the structure: ExpandoObject enables adding and deleting members of an instance at run time and setting/getting their values, binds them through the dynamic keyword (sampleObject.sampleMember instead of a GetAttribute call), implements IDictionary<string, object> for enumeration and deletion, and raises INotifyPropertyChanged so bound UI updates when a member changes. Derive from DynamicObject when a name must mean more than a dictionary entry - override TryGetMember/TrySetMember/GetDynamicMemberNames, which also makes members visible to tooling - and use [JsonExtensionData] on typed models to capture unknown JSON members instead of dropping them. Keep real properties where the name set is fixed: dynamic members get no IntelliSense, no compiler checking, and a typo only throws at runtime.
pitfalls: Members reached through dynamic are bound at run time: a typo compiles and throws RuntimeBinderException, and the docs note there is no IntelliSense and no compiler error for non-existent members.

ExpandoObject has no shared schema - two instances can carry different key sets - so deserializing untrusted payloads into it lets any key become a member; validate against an allow-list, and prefer DynamicObject when names must be checked.

Enumeration and deletion need the IDictionary<string, object> view, and data binding needs INotifyPropertyChanged or DynamicObject member-name reporting; a bag that skips both looks empty to the UI and to serializers.
